newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Trades lower on softer crude.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Trades lower on softer crude.

text.p: Singapore gas oil and jet fuel markets were weaker on Tuesday along with softer crude values, traders said.
They said the market is entering a low demand period with few enquiries seen in the region while supplies remained abundant.
China was weighed down by ample supplies as refineries return from scheduled shutdowns while congestions at the Fujian port of Xiamen continued to cause market jitters.
At latest count, traders said about 11 gas oil vessels of 30,000 tonnes each were waiting to discharge cargoes, with some vessels already said to be turning away.
Several cargoes were now heard to be offered into Hong Kong, which some traders said was an unusual phenomenon.

They noted that if the cargoes were sold to Hong Kong, they would eventually have to end up in southern China, which made it less attractive for majors in Hong Kong to buy in the light of the current ample supply situation on the mainland.
Indonesia was said to have covered most of its purchases for June gas oil, estimated around four million barrels, while jet fuel was estimated at least at 1.5 milliion barrels.

Gas oil was traded lower with two cargoes purchased by a Japanese trader at $25.35 per barrel free-on-board--one cargo from a European major for June 15-19, and another from another European major for June 4-8 lifting.

Jet fuel also traded much lower with a European major selling two cargoes--a Japanese trader bought 26,000 tonnes at $24.25 per barrel for June 4-8 and a Singapore trader bought at $24.60 for June 15-19 lifting fob basis.
The traded levels were 40-75 cents below Monday's deal.
Traders said jet fuel supplies are abundant in the region while demand is slow.
